summary: Defines an RTCP Extended Report block type for multicast acquisition. Receivers that join a multicast RTP session often face a delay before they can use the data, and this report block helps measure how well rapid acquisition methods perform.

eli5.summary: When you tune into a live show, you may have to wait before the picture makes sense. This adds a report that lets receivers tell the sender how long that wait was.

questions: what is the rtcp multicast acquisition report block
what is rtcp xr block type 11
subtitle: A report block that lets multicast receivers tell the network operator how long it took them to start getting data.

tldr.problem: Receivers that join a multicast RTP session often cannot use the data right away, and operators have no standard way to learn how long each receiver waited or why.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6332 defines the Multicast Acquisition (MA) report block, an RTCP Extended Report block (type 11) with a status code and optional timing fields, plus an SDP parameter to signal it.
tldr.outcome: Operators can collect and compare acquisition experiences across receivers and across methods such as simple join and RAMS. It is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted.

today: RFC 6332 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Report Multicast Acquisition
sections.content:
In many multicast applications, such as video, the RTP source sends inter-related data. A receiver that joins at a random moment may not be able to decode a packet until it has earlier packets or some Reference Information about the content. The result is a random acquisition delay.

RFC 6285 reduces this delay with Rapid Acquisition of Multicast RTP Sessions (RAMS). A retransmission server sends the Reference Information to the joining receiver over an auxiliary unicast RTP session. Performance still varies between receivers and over time, because it depends on group management processing times, network resources and the nature of the data.

RFC 6332 adds a way to measure this. Receivers using RAMS, another rapid acquisition method, or a plain multicast join can all send the report each time they join a new multicast session. The service provider can then quantitatively compare the methods.
sections.eli5: Joining a live stream can mean waiting a bit before it makes sense. This lets each viewer report how long the wait was, so the TV company can see which tricks work best.

sections.title: The Base Report
sections.content:
The MA report block is carried inside an RTCP Extended Report (XR) packet, whose payload type is 207. It is only sent as part of an RTCP compound packet, and it is sent in the primary multicast session. The RFC advises sending it only after all the information has been collected, since partial reports are not useful and complicate matching. It may be repeated for redundancy while respecting RTCP scheduling. All integer fields are in network byte order.

The base report has these fields:

  • BT (8 bits): the block type, the constant 11.
  • MA Method (8 bits): the acquisition method, such as simple join or RAMS.
  • Block Length (16 bits): the length of the block including the header, in 32-bit words minus one.
  • SSRC of the Primary Multicast Stream (32 bits).
  • Status (16 bits): the status code for the acquisition attempt.
  • Rsvd. (16 bits): the receiver MUST set it to zero and the recipient MUST ignore it.

If the join succeeded, meaning at least one multicast packet was received, extra information MUST be appended as described in the extensions.
sections.eli5: The base report is a short form with a few boxes to fill in: which stream, which method, and how it went.

sections.title: Status Codes
sections.content:
The Status field says how the attempt went. Codes are grouped by method: values 1 to 1000 are primarily for simple join, and 1001 to 2000 are for the RAMS method. Examples are 1 (multicast join was successful), 2 (join has failed), 3 (a presentation error) and 1001 (RAMS has been successfully completed). The status code reported MUST be within the scope of the method named in the MA Method field.

For RAMS, RFC 6285 defines response codes. If the receiver gets a 1xx or 2xx response code, it MUST use one of the 1xxx status codes. If it gets a 4xx or 5xx code (receiver-side and server-side errors), it MUST report that response code as its status, so these have higher priority.

A status of zero means a private extension is in use. A private extension MUST NOT be used unless the receiver knows out of band that the entity processing the report understands it.
sections.eli5: The status is a number that says what happened, like a score card: it worked, it failed, or something went wrong on the way.

sections.title: TLV Extensions
sections.content:
More fields are added after the base report as TLV (type, length, value) elements. Each has a one-octet Type, a one-octet Reserved field set to zero, a two-octet Length (in octets, excluding the Type, Reserved and Length fields and any padding) and a Value. An element that does not end on a 32-bit boundary is padded with zero bits.

The vendor-neutral elements usable by any RTP multicast application are the RTP sequence number of the first multicast packet (type 1), the SFGMP join time (type 2), the application request-to-multicast delta time (type 3) and the application request-to-presentation delta time (type 4). Types 1 and 2 MUST be included when the join succeeded. Times are in milliseconds.

When the receiver used RAMS and sent a rapid acquisition request, further optional elements (types 11 to 17) report timings between the request, the RAMS Information message, the burst and the first multicast packet, plus the number of duplicate packets and the size of the burst-to-multicast gap. If no rapid acquisition request was sent, these elements MUST NOT appear. Many elements MUST NOT appear when the packet they measure was never received.

Types 128 to 254 are reserved for private extensions, which add a 32-bit enterprise number after the header so vendors do not collide.
sections.eli5: Extra boxes can be stapled on after the base form, such as stopwatch times. Companies can also add their own boxes, marked with their company number.

sections.title: Signaling in SDP
sections.content: A new unilateral parameter, multicast-acq, is defined for the rtcp-xr attribute of the Session Description Protocol. It extends the xr-format rule from RFC 3611 using ABNF. The full syntax of the attribute is described in Section 5.1 of RFC 3611.
sections.eli5: A session description can include a note saying that this kind of report is in use, like a label on the box.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 3611 apply. Like other RTCP reports, MA reports could be stolen without protection, and they can reveal performance characteristics of the RTP service and network. Reports MAY be protected with SRTP and SRTCP (RFC 3711), and the RFC RECOMMENDS SRTCP for integrity protection.

If reports feed back into later acquisition attempts, forged or modified reports can cause harm. For example, incorrectly small SFGMP join times could make a unicast burst too short, leaving gaps in sequence numbers. Forged reports could also make rapid acquisition look healthy when it is failing, or the reverse. Private extensions may carry data an attacker could not otherwise see.
sections.eli5: If someone sends fake report cards, the TV company might make wrong choices. Locking the reports so nobody can change them helps.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
IANA registered block type 11 for the Multicast Acquisition Report Block in the RTCP XR Block Type Registry, and the SDP parameter multicast-acq. It also created three registries managed under the Specification Required policy.

  • Multicast Acquisition Method Registry: 1 is simple join, 2 is RAMS, 0 and 255 are reserved, and 3 to 254 are unassigned.
  • TLV Space Registry: types 1 to 4 and 11 to 17 as above, 5 to 10 and 18 to 127 unassigned, 128 to 254 private, 0 and 255 reserved.
  • Status Code Space Registry: codes as described earlier, and 65535 reserved.

A registration for an unassigned value must include contact information and a detailed description.
sections.eli5: There is an official list that gives each method, box and status number its meaning, so everyone uses the same numbers.

viz.caption: BASE REPORT FORMAT FOR THE MA REPORT BLOCK

fields.name: Block Length
fields.desc: Block length in 32-bit words minus one, including the header.

fields.name: SSRC of the Primary Multicast Stream
fields.desc: SSRC of the primary multicast stream.

fields.name: Status
fields.desc: Status code for the MA operation.

fields.name: Rsvd.
fields.desc: Set to zero by the sender and ignored by the recipient.

items.label: Private
items.desc: A private status code is included in the message.

items.label: Join successful
items.desc: Multicast join was successful.

items.label: Join failed
items.desc: Multicast join has failed.

items.label: Presentation error
items.desc: A presentation error has occurred.

items.label: Internal error
items.desc: An unspecified RTP receiver internal error has occurred.

items.label: RAMS completed
items.desc: RAMS has been successfully completed.

items.label: No RAMS-R sent
items.desc: No RAMS-R message has been sent.

items.label: Invalid RAMS-I
items.desc: Invalid RAMS-I message syntax.

items.label: RAMS-I timeout
items.desc: RAMS-I message has timed out.

items.label: Burst timeout
items.desc: RAMS unicast burst has timed out.

items.label: RAMS internal error
items.desc: Unspecified RTP receiver internal error during RAMS.

items.label: RAMS presentation error
items.desc: A presentation error has occurred during RAMS.

items.label: First multicast seqnum
items.desc: RTP sequence number of the first multicast packet (16 bits).

items.label: SFGMP join time
items.desc: Milliseconds from sending the join to the first multicast packet (32 bits).

items.label: App request to multicast
items.desc: Application request to first primary multicast packet.

items.label: App request to presentation
items.desc: Application request to first presentation of the media.

items.label: App request to RAMS request
items.desc: Application request to sending the rapid acquisition request.

items.label: RAMS request to RAMS info
items.desc: Request sent to first RAMS Information message received.

items.label: RAMS request to burst
items.desc: Request sent to first burst packet received.

items.label: RAMS request to multicast
items.desc: Request sent to first primary multicast packet received.

items.label: RAMS request to burst end
items.desc: Request sent to last burst packet received.

items.label: Duplicate packets
items.desc: Packets received in both the unicast and multicast sessions.

items.label: Burst-to-multicast gap
items.desc: Gap between the last burst packet and the first multicast packet.
